extensionName.description: Name of the extension, used as the logo alt text

extensionDescription.message: Protection against lookalike and impersonation sites (homograph attacks & clone phishing) based on your personal visit history

securityWarning.description: Title of the security warning popup

inputWarningMessage.message: You're entering text on an unfamiliar site. Before you give it a password or card details, open Visilant from your browser's toolbar or extensions menu and make sure it's the site you think it is.

copyAction.description: Button beside an address or a QR code's text that puts it on the clipboard

copyDone.description: The copy button right after it worked

copyFailed.description: The copy button failed, usually because the page or the browser does not allow it

copyWarningMessage.message: Something was just copied on an unfamiliar site, and it may not be what you selected. Look at it before you paste it anywhere important.
copyWarningMessage.description: Warning message for copy/cut actions, and for a site writing to the clipboard by itself

avoidShell.message: If the site tells you to press some keys and then paste, for example into a Run box or a terminal, don't. That runs a command that can take over your computer.
avoidShell.description: Security tip about not pasting into shell

verifyContent.message: To see what you really copied, paste it into a note first.
verifyContent.description: Security tip about verifying copied content

warningSilenceHint.message: To turn these warnings off for this site, open Visilant from your browser's toolbar or extensions menu. If a site asks you to turn them off, it's a scam.
warningSilenceHint.description: Line in the in-page warning saying where the per-site silence lives. Deliberately not a button, so a page cannot talk the reader into silencing itself in one click.

onThisPage.description: Heading of the settings page table of contents

generalSettings.description: Title for general settings section, in a table of contents where every entry is a section of the settings

familiaritySettings.description: Title of the familiarity rules section

familiarityIntro.message: When a site counts as familiar. Warnings, the icon colour, link checks and the paste hold all follow this verdict.
familiarityIntro.description: Intro text for the familiarity section

familiarityVisitsDesc.message: Times you used the site. A page counts once you click, tap, type or scroll on it, not for loading or reloading, and visits within a minute of each other count as 1.

familiarityActiveDaysDesc.message: Separate days you were there. Ten visits in one afternoon are 1 day.

familiarityAge.description: Title of the first-visit age criterion. Named for what it counts, like the two beside it – a column of bare numbers under it then needs no unit repeated on every row

familiarityVisitsCompact.description: The visit-count criterion as one sentence, used when explanations are switched off. {n} is where the number box goes, and may sit anywhere in the sentence.

familiarityActiveDaysCompact.description: The active-days criterion as one sentence, used when explanations are switched off. {n} is where the number box goes.

familiarityAgeCompact.description: The first-visit age criterion as one sentence, used when explanations are switched off. {n} is where the number box goes.

familiarityAgeDesc.message: Days since your first recorded visit.
familiarityAgeDesc.description: Description of the first-visit age criterion

familiarityAtLeastLabel.description: Prefix for a criterion threshold input

familiarityDaysUnit.description: Unit after a threshold counted in days

familiarityRequiredAtLeast.description: Tooltip prefix showing what a criterion asks for

familiarityModeLabel.message: How many checks have to pass
familiarityModeLabel.description: Label for the familiarity mode select

familiarityModeAny.description: Familiarity mode: a single criterion is enough

familiarityModeAtLeast.description: Familiarity mode: a chosen number of criteria

familiarityModeAtLeastLabel.description: Label for the number of criteria required

familiarityKeepOne.message: At least one check has to stay on.
familiarityKeepOne.description: Why the last enabled checkbox cannot be cleared

familiarityShowThresholds.description: Setting label for showing thresholds next to familiarity facts

familiarityShowThresholdsDesc.message: Shows the number each check needs beside the site's own number.
familiarityShowThresholdsDesc.description: What the threshold display option controls

familiarityFactCheck.description: Column heading for the familiarity check being reported

familiarityFactValue.description: Column heading for what the site actually has

familiarityFactNeeded.description: Column heading for the threshold a check has to clear

familiarityNeedsImportTitle.message: Some sites have no dates on record
familiarityNeedsImportTitle.description: Title of the warning about records missing the newer fields

familiarityNeedsImportText.message: sites have no active days or first-visit date on record, so they fail those checks. A full history import fills them in.
familiarityNeedsImportText.description: Body of the warning about records missing the newer fields

familiarityNeedsImportLink.description: Link from the familiarity section to the import controls

displaySettingsPinNote.message: Both settings need the Visilant icon pinned to the browser's toolbar.
displaySettingsPinNote.description: Note explaining that the icon settings require the extension icon to be pinned

displaySettingsPinNoteAndroid.message: This browser keeps the Visilant icon in its menu, under Extensions. Both settings draw on it there.
displaySettingsPinNoteAndroid.description: Replaces the pin-to-toolbar note on Firefox for Android, where the extension icon lives in the browser menu

dynamicIconDesc.message: Red on an unfamiliar site, grey on an unfamiliar site whose warnings you turned off.

badgeContentLabel.description: Label of the select that picks the number drawn on the icon

badgeContentDesc.message: Which number the counter shows. Its colour follows the verdict, and is grey on an unfamiliar site whose warnings you turned off. A check switched off in the familiarity rules isn't offered.
badgeContentDesc.description: Description of the badge content select

badgeContentActiveDays.description: Badge shows the number of separate days the site was visited

badgeContentAge.description: Badge shows how long ago the first visit was

badgeContentChecks.description: Badge shows how many familiarity checks the site passes, as 2/3

showBadgeDesc.message: A number for the current site, drawn on the icon.

showWarningNotificationDesc.message: Only on unfamiliar sites, and only at the moments chosen below.

browserNotificationsDesc.message: Shown by your system, outside the page, where no site can touch them. Do-not-disturb mode silences them.

inPageNotificationsDesc.message: Drawn on the page itself. Your system can't silence it, but a fake site can try to hide it.

bothNotifications.description: Option for both types of notifications

notificationStylePinNote.message: Either way, the Visilant icon is outside every page, so no site can silence it, remove it or draw a fake over it. On a computer, keep it pinned to the toolbar.
notificationStylePinNote.description: Note below the notification style options, recommending the pinned icon as the indicator a site cannot fake

importHistoryIntro.message: Your browser history is read on this device to learn which sites you already use. Nothing is sent anywhere.
importHistoryIntro.description: Note above the manual import buttons, explaining the automatic import already ran

importStatusNever.message: Nothing imported yet. Run the import below.
importStatusNever.description: Import status: nothing has ever been imported

importStatusRunning.message: An import is running right now.
importStatusRunning.description: Import status: an import is in flight right now

importStatusComplete.description: Import status: everything imported, dates included

importStatusPartial.message: Visit counts are in, but first-visit dates and active days aren't. Run the import to fill them in.
importStatusPartial.description: Import status: counts imported but no full pass ever finished

importStatusInterrupted.message: An import was cut short and hasn't been picked up again. Run the import to finish it, it continues from where it stopped.
importStatusInterrupted.description: Import status: an import was cut short and never resumed

importStatusCancelled.message: The import was stopped before it finished. Visit counts may be incomplete, so run it again.
importStatusCancelled.description: Import status: the user stopped the import

importStatusFailed.message: The last import ended with an error. Run the import to try again.
importStatusFailed.description: Import status: the import ended in an error

importStatusUnsupported.message: This browser gives extensions no history to read, so there's nothing to import. Sites become familiar as you visit them.
importStatusUnsupported.description: Import status: the browser has no history API, as on Firefox for Android

importLastRun.description: Label for the date of the last history import

importSitesStored.description: Unit after the number of sites stored by the last import

importHistoryRun.description: Label for the history import button

importHistoryFirstRun.description: Label for the same button while nothing has been imported yet, so there is nothing to re-do

importHistoryRunDesc.message: Safe to repeat: counts are matched, not added up. A large history takes a while, and you can cancel without losing what was already read.
importHistoryRunDesc.description: Description of the history import button

statsUnknown.description: Shown instead of a date that the extension cannot know

statsNoneYet.description: In the comparison table, in place of a fact (active days, days known) about a site that has never been visited. Not "not recorded", which reads as a failure to record something that happened, and not "none yet", which reads as a promise that the reader will go there

statsImportHint.message: Import your browser history to fill this in
statsImportHint.description: Hint shown when first-visit data is missing

untrackedHostBadge.description: Badge shown instead of a familiar/unfamiliar verdict for an address that is never counted

untrackedHostTitle.description: Heading of the notice shown for a name that only works inside one network (localhost, printer.lan)

untrackedHostText.message: A name like localhost or printer.lan works inside one network only. Nobody can register it on the internet, so it can't be a fake of another site. Visilant keeps no count for it and never warns about it.
untrackedHostText.description: Explains why a local name (no dot, or a suffix like .lan) has no visit count and never triggers a warning

untrackedIpBadge.description: Badge shown instead of a familiar/unfamiliar verdict for a private IP address, which is never counted

untrackedIpTitle.message: This is an IP address, not a domain name
untrackedIpTitle.description: Heading of the notice shown for a private IP address such as 192.168.1.1

untrackedIpText.message: An address on a private network, such as your home router. Nobody on the internet can own it, so Visilant keeps no count for it and never warns about it.
untrackedIpText.description: Explains why a private IP address has no visit count and never triggers a warning

visitsInfo.description: Label for visit information reset option

allSettings.description: Label for all settings reset option

confirmResetMessage.message: Are you sure you want to reset the following data?

showInputWarningDesc.message: The last moment a warning can stop a password, card number or code from going to the wrong site.

showCopyWarning.message: When copying, or when a site copies something for you

showCopyWarningDesc.message: What lands in the clipboard can differ from what you selected, for example a command meant for a terminal. Also covers a site copying something by itself when you press one of its buttons.

bothWarningTriggers.description: Label for both warning trigger events option

blockPasteOnUnfamiliar.description: Label of the setting that holds a paste until confirmed

blockPasteOnUnfamiliarDesc.message: The first paste on an unfamiliar site is held so you can look at the address. Allow it, paste again, and the page stops asking. Works whether or not the warnings above are on.
blockPasteOnUnfamiliarDesc.description: What the paste hold does and what it cannot do

pasteInterceptTitle.description: Title of the paste confirmation dialog

pasteInterceptMessage.message: Nothing was pasted. This is an unfamiliar site: if it's a password, a card number or a code, first make sure this is the site you meant to open.
pasteInterceptMessage.description: Body of the paste confirmation dialog

pasteInterceptRepeatHint.message: "Allow pasting" lets your next paste through. Paste again after you press it, and you won't be asked again on this page.
pasteInterceptRepeatHint.description: Explains that allowing does not paste, the user pastes again themselves

pasteInterceptAllow.description: Button that lets the paste through

pasteInterceptReveal.description: Button that shows the clipboard contents

pasteInterceptHide.description: Button that hides the clipboard contents again

pasteInterceptChars.description: Unit after the number of characters on the clipboard

pasteInterceptKindText.description: Clipboard contents look like ordinary text

pasteInterceptKindUrl.description: Clipboard contents look like a web address

pasteInterceptKindEmail.description: Clipboard contents look like an email address

pasteInterceptKindDigits.message: Digits, such as a card number or a code
pasteInterceptKindDigits.description: Clipboard contents look like a number, card or code

warningTriggerEventsTitle.description: Title for warning trigger events section

checkedDomain.description: Heading of the domain card when the popup is opened as its own tab, where there is no current domain

relatedDomains.description: Header for the list of recorded hostnames under the base domain. Not "Subdomains": the list holds every name at any depth, the base domain itself among them, and that one is nobody's subdomain

foldTotal.description: Appended to a heading over a family figure that is the sum of every host under the domain. Only visits add up

foldMax.description: Appended to a heading over a family figure taken from the strongest single host rather than a sum – active days, age and passed checks, none of which can be added together

familySummaryTitle.message: All addresses on this site, together
familySummaryTitle.description: Small label over the row of facts on the base domain card, saying the numbers under it summarise every host in the list below rather than describing one address

shortenerHostNotice.message: Short-link service: its links can lead to any site, so your visit history here says nothing about where they lead.
shortenerHostNotice.description: Warning line on the domain card of the popup when the domain is on the shortener list. The figures stay, since they are true about the site itself, but they say nothing about where its links go

familyOnlyCheckedDomain.message: Nothing else is recorded on this site.
familyOnlyCheckedDomain.description: Line on the base domain card where the family's figures would be, when the address in the Checked domain card above is the only one recorded under it. Says the figures are missing because there is nothing to add up, not because they were forgotten. Names that card by its heading

listNumberLabel.description: Label before the chips picking which number the subdomain list draws, and the same word on the sort button when the list is ordered by that number. The chips themselves are named after the familiarity checks, since they are the same facts

listShowLabel.description: Label before the dropdown that picks which number each row of the related-address list shows

listSortLabel.description: Label before the two buttons setting the order of the subdomain list

sortByName.description: The sort button's other state: the list ordered by hostname rather than by the number on show

sortToName.message: Sort by name – currently by the number shown
sortToName.description: Tooltip on that button while the list is ordered by its number

sortToNumber.message: Sort by the number shown – currently by name
sortToNumber.description: Tooltip on that button while the list is ordered by name

firstVisitOn.description: Hover text before the date a number of days since the first visit was measured from

sortOrderToAsc.description: Sort button tooltip while sorting descending

sortOrderToDesc.description: Sort button tooltip while sorting ascending

caseToUpper.description: Case button tooltip while showing lowercase

caseToLower.description: Case button tooltip while showing uppercase

punycodeShowAscii.message: Show the coded form (punycode) – currently the readable form
punycodeShowAscii.description: Domain format button tooltip while showing the original

punycodeShowUnicode.message: Show the readable form – currently the coded form (punycode)
punycodeShowUnicode.description: Domain format button tooltip while showing punycode

domainOriginal.description: Label for the unicode domain version

domainPunycode.description: Label for the punycode domain version

current.description: Label for current domain in list

noVisitData.message: No visits recorded on this site yet.
noVisitData.description: Message when no data is found

visitWebsite.message: Open a site to see what Visilant knows about it

tamperingMessage.message: This page tried to hide Visilant's warnings. Fake sites do this, and some real sites do it by accident. Before you type anything here, open Visilant from your browser's toolbar or extensions menu and check the site.
tamperingMessage.description: Message shown when tampering is detected

linkSafetySettings.description: Title for link safety settings section

linkSafetySettingsDesc.message: Shows where a link leads before you open it.

linkSafetyEnabled.description: Label for link safety master toggle

linkTooltipTrigger.description: Heading over the ways to see what a link leads to without opening it (hover, right click). Stopping a click is a separate setting below it

linkTooltipTriggerHoverDesc.message: Appears when the pointer rests on a link. If short links are followed at once, the link is requested at that moment.

linkHoverDelay.message: Delay before the link check appears
linkHoverDelay.description: Label of the hover delay slider

linkHoverDelayDesc.message: How long the pointer has to rest on a link.
linkHoverDelayDesc.description: What the hover delay changes and how to pick it

linkHoverDelaySeconds.description: Unit shown next to the hover delay value

linkHoverDelayInstant.description: Value shown when the hover delay is zero

linkTooltipTriggerClickRight.description: Tooltip trigger option: right click via context menu

linkTooltipTriggerClickRightDesc.message: Right-clicking a link shows "Check this link" in the context menu.
linkTooltipTriggerClickRightDesc.description: Description for right click trigger option

linkTooltipTriggerHoverUnavailable.message: Unavailable on a phone: there's no pointer to rest on a link.
linkTooltipTriggerHoverUnavailable.description: Shown under the hover trigger on touch devices, where it can never fire

linkTooltipTriggerClickRightUnavailable.message: Unavailable in Firefox for Android: it doesn't let extensions add items to the long-press menu.
linkTooltipTriggerClickRightUnavailable.description: Shown under the right-click trigger on Firefox for Android, which has no menus API

linkTooltipTriggerTouchNote.message: This device has no pointer to hover with and no right-click, so the link check shows only for a link that is stopped. Which links are stopped is set below.
linkTooltipTriggerTouchNote.description: Shown above the trigger options on touch devices, where only the tap trigger can fire

linkTooltipTriggerNoMenusNote.message: This browser doesn't let extensions add items to the long-press menu, so the check shows when the pointer rests on a link instead.
linkTooltipTriggerNoMenusNote.description: Shown under the link-check trigger where a pointer exists but the menus API does not, as on Firefox for Android with a mouse attached

linkShowVisitCount.message: Show the familiarity facts when checking links
linkShowVisitCount.description: Setting label for visit count display mode

linkShowVisitCountDesc.message: When a link check also lists the facts behind its verdict: visits, active days and days known.

linkShowVisitCountAlways.description: Show visit count for all links

linkShowVisitCountUnfamiliar.description: Show visit count only for unfamiliar sites

linkShowVisitCountFamiliar.description: Show visit count only for familiar sites

linkShortUrlSection.description: Section header for shortened URL settings

linkShortUrlModeButton.message: Follow when you press the button

linkShortUrlModeButtonDesc.message: Nothing is requested until you press the button on the link check.
linkShortUrlModeButtonDesc.description: What resolving on button click means

linkShortUrlModeAutoDesc.message: Every short link you look at is requested at once, the last site on its way too, whether or not you click it.

linkShortUrlShowFullUrl.message: Show the whole address it leads to, not only the site
linkShortUrlShowFullUrl.description: Toggle to show full URL vs domain only

linkShortUrlTraceChain.message: Show every step on the way
linkShortUrlTraceChain.description: Toggle to show full redirect hop chain

linkShortUrlResolveAny.message: Offer to follow any link, not only known short links
linkShortUrlResolveAny.description: Toggle to enable resolving any link

linkShortUrlResolveAnyDesc.message: For a short-link service the built-in list misses. With "Follow at once", every link you look at is then requested.

linkShortUrlListUpdateUrl.description: Label for remote list URLs textarea

linkShortUrlListUpdateUrlDesc.message: One address per line, each a plain-text list of short-link services. Downloaded when you press the button.

linkScopeModeDesc.message: Where links are checked. Every site is recommended, since an unexpected link can turn up anywhere.
linkScopeModeDesc.description: What the scope option is for

linkScopeDomains.description: Placeholder for scope domain list textarea

linkScopeDomainsNote.description: Note that the scope domain list matches subdomains too

linkTooltipFamiliar.description: Label for familiar/safe site in tooltip

linkTooltipUnfamiliar.description: Label for unfamiliar/unsafe site in tooltip

linkTooltipMismatchWarning.message: The link shows one site but leads to another.
linkTooltipMismatchWarning.description: Warning about mismatched link text and href

linkTooltipShowsDomain.description: Prefix for the domain shown in link text

linkTooltipLeadsTo.description: Prefix for the actual destination domain

addressMeantToReadAs.description: Label straight under an address in its coded xn-- form, before the readable name that address was made to be shown as. Not a warning, only what the coded address stands for

domainMarkerUserinfo.description: Marker: URL contains userinfo before the host

domainMarkerIpHost.message: IP address, not a domain name
domainMarkerIpHost.description: Marker: host is a raw IP address

domainMarkerHostedOn.message: {platform} lets anyone make a site there. This one isn't run by the platform itself.
domainMarkerHostedOn.description: Marker on an unfamiliar site that is one of many on a shared hosting platform, as in alice.github.io. {platform} is the platform's address (github.io), drawn as an address. Its point is that the famous name in the address says nothing about who made this site

domainMarkerEmbeddedSuffix.message: Made to look like {domain} but the real site is {site}
domainMarkerEmbeddedSuffix.description: Marker: a whole domain in the middle of the address, as in yourbank.com.pay-verify.top. {domain} is the domain the address is dressed as (yourbank.com), or several of them, each joined to the next with listOr and never with a comma, which beside an address reads as one of its dots, {site} is the site it belongs to (pay-verify.top). All are drawn as addresses

domainMarkerDeepSubdomains.description: Marker: subdomain nesting deeper than usual

domainMarkerMixedScripts.message: Different alphabets in one part of the address
domainMarkerMixedScripts.description: Marker: a hostname label mixes writing systems

domainMarkerLatinTwins.message: Only {alphabet} letters that look like Latin ones
domainMarkerLatinTwins.description: Red flag: a part of the address is written entirely in letters of another alphabet that look like Latin letters, as аррӏе.com in Cyrillic. {alphabet} is the alphabet's name. The part follows after a colon

domainMarkerLatinTwinsWhy.message: It reads as a Latin name, but it's a different address.
domainMarkerLatinTwinsWhy.description: Second sentence after the Latin-twins red flag

domainMarkerNonLatin.description: Red flag: a part of the address is in another alphabet while the address ends in Latin letters, as пример.com. {alphabet} is the alphabet's name, {name} the part in that alphabet and {ending} the ending, both drawn in frames. No comma or full stop may stand straight after either: beside a piece of an address it reads as a dot of the address

domainMarkerOtherEnding.message: {alphabet} letters {name} before the ending {ending} in {endingAlphabet} letters
domainMarkerOtherEnding.description: Red flag: a part of the address is in one alphabet while the address ends in another non-Latin one, as a Greek name under .рф. {alphabet} and {endingAlphabet} are alphabet names, {name} the part and {ending} the ending, both drawn in frames with no punctuation straight after them

domainMarkerOtherEndingUnnamed.message: {alphabet} letters {name} before the ending {ending} in another alphabet
domainMarkerOtherEndingUnnamed.description: Red flag: as domainMarkerOtherEnding, for an ending in an alphabet Visilant has no name for. {alphabet} is the name part's alphabet, {name} the part and {ending} the ending, both drawn in frames with no punctuation straight after them

domainMarkerNonLatinWhy.message: Visilant expects a name and its ending to be written in the same alphabet.
domainMarkerNonLatinWhy.description: Second sentence after the non-Latin-name red flag, saying what Visilant expects instead

domainMarkerNonLatinWhyExamples.message: Visilant expects a name in {alphabet} letters under an ending written the same way, such as {examples}
domainMarkerNonLatinWhyExamples.description: The same sentence with examples: {examples} are national endings in that alphabet, for instance .рф for Cyrillic

scriptCyrillic.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptGreek.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptArmenian.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptGeorgian.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptHebrew.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptArabic.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptDevanagari.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptBengali.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptThai.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptCjk.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

scriptOther.description: Name of an alphabet, inside the red flag about a name in another alphabet

lookalikeWhoFamiliar.description: Fills {who} in the lookalike sentences when the imitated domain comes from the user's own history

lookalikeWhoProvider.description: Fills {who} in the lookalike sentences when the imitated domain comes from the built-in mail provider list, which the user may never have visited

lookalikeReasonConfusable.message: May be made to look like {who} {site} with some characters swapped for lookalike ones
lookalikeReasonConfusable.description: Lookalike warning, one sentence. Says "may be", not "is": honest sites can look alike, so it points out the resemblance without accusing anyone. {who} is lookalikeWhoFamiliar or lookalikeWhoProvider, {site} is the imitated domain, drawn highlighted. The address uses letters from another alphabet or digits that look like the real letters

lookalikeReasonEditDistance.message: May be made to look like {who} {site} with a letter or two changed
lookalikeReasonEditDistance.description: Lookalike warning, one sentence. {who} and {site} as in lookalikeReasonConfusable. The address is one or two typos away from the real name

lookalikeReasonContains.message: May be made to look like {who} {site} with extra text added
lookalikeReasonContains.description: Lookalike warning, one sentence. {who} and {site} as in lookalikeReasonConfusable. The address holds the real name with more text around it, like paypal-secure.com

lookalikeReasonSubdomain.message: May be made to look like {who} {site} but the real site is {real}
lookalikeReasonSubdomain.description: Lookalike warning, one sentence. {who} and {site} as in lookalikeReasonConfusable, {real} is the site the address really belongs to, drawn as an address. The real name sits in front of somebody else's domain, like paypal.com.evil.net, where {real} is evil.net

lookalikeReasonSameName.message: May be made to look like {who} {site} with a different ending
lookalikeReasonSameName.description: Lookalike warning, one sentence. {who} and {site} as in lookalikeReasonConfusable. The same name under another domain ending, like paypal.co next to paypal.com

verdictUnchecked.description: Verdict badge when Visilant could not look the site up at all, for example right after the extension was updated and the page has not been reloaded. Not a judgement about the site

linkInterceptTitleUnchecked.description: Title of the navigation dialog when Visilant could not look the destination up at all. Says nothing about the site itself

linkUncheckedNotice.message: Visilant couldn't check this site just now, so it can't say whether you've visited it before. Reloading the page usually fixes this.
linkUncheckedNotice.description: Shown instead of the visit facts when the check could not run. The usual cause is a page left open across an extension update

linkInterceptOpen.description: Link dialog for a held click, when the destination is familiar and nothing was found: the button that opens the link

linkInterceptOpenNewTab.description: Button that opens the link in a new tab: in the link dialog and the link tooltip when they were opened from the menu, where nobody clicked the link

linkInterceptAllowLink.description: Link dialog, for a link inside a frame from another site: the button opens nothing, it lets the next click on that link through

mismatchVisitsHidden.description: Shown in mismatch table when visit count is hidden per user settings

linkInterceptTitleHidden.description: Title of the navigation dialog when the link goes through a known shortener that has not been resolved

linkInterceptTitleFamiliar.description: Title of the navigation dialog when the destination is familiar

linkInterceptPhishingHint.message: If you meant to go to a site you use, this may be a fake made to steal your password or money. Open that site the way you usually do, from a bookmark or by typing its address.
linkInterceptPhishingHint.description: Hint in the navigation dialog for an unfamiliar destination

linkInterceptDomainInfo.description: Button that opens the site in Visilant's own window, in a new tab (link and paste dialogs)

linkInterceptContinue.description: Link dialog for a held click: the button that opens the link in spite of what the dialog says. Pairs with Don't open

linkInterceptStatus.description: Row label for familiarity status in mismatch comparison table

linkTooltipDestination.description: Label for destination domain in tooltip

linkContextMenuCheckDomain.message: Site details in a new tab
linkContextMenuCheckDomain.description: Context menu item on a link: opens what Visilant knows about the link's site in a new tab, the same page the Site details button opens

linkContextMenuCheckLink.description: Context menu item to check link safety (shows intercept dialog)

linkTooltipShortener.description: Label indicating a URL shortener domain

linkTooltipShortenedUrl.description: Heading over the address a followed link ended at, on the tooltip and in the dialog

linkTooltipResolvingUrl.description: Loading state while resolving shortened URL

linkTooltipResolveRefused.message: This link leads into your own network, to a router or a computer near you. Visilant stops following a link there, so where it ends isn't known.
linkTooltipResolveRefused.description: Shown instead of a destination when following a short link would mean a request into the local network

linkTooltipResolveError.message: Couldn't find where this link leads
linkTooltipResolveError.description: Error state when URL resolution fails

linkTooltipResolveSameDomain.message: Visilant followed the link and it stayed on the same site.
linkTooltipResolveSameDomain.description: A link that is not on the shortener list was followed and stayed on the same site

linkTooltipResolveSameDomainShortener.message: Couldn't find where this short link leads. It may be broken, or the service blocked the check.
linkTooltipResolveSameDomainShortener.description: A known shortener was followed but did not lead anywhere else

linkResolveTry.message: Try to find where it leads
linkResolveTry.description: The one button that follows a link to see where it ends, on a known short link and on any other link alike. It says "try" because following can fail, which the question mark beside it explains

linkShortUrlSectionWarning.message: Following a short link requests every site it passes through, the last one too. Each sees a visit from your internet address, and a link that works only once may stop working. No page is drawn, no script runs.

linkResolveHelp.message: Visilant opens the link itself, in the background, as a visitor who isn't signed in to anything. None of your logins are sent, but every site the link passes through, the last one too, sees a visit from your internet address. A link that does something as soon as it's opened, like one to confirm an email or to unsubscribe, will have done it. A link that works only once may no longer work for you. Sometimes Visilant can't tell where a link leads, because the page has to be opened in a real browser first.

addressSpellingHelp.message: An address with letters other than plain Latin a to z has two forms: the readable one and a coded one with xn-- in it, called punycode. It's one address. Letters of another alphabet can look exactly like Latin ones, which lets a fake site look exactly like one you know. On a site in that language, an xn-- address is normal.

linkInterceptCancel.description: The safe way out of the link dialog: closes it and the link is not opened. Not 'Go back': nobody has gone anywhere yet

statusChecking.description: Badge while Visilant is still looking a site up

popupTextSize.description: Label of the group of text size buttons in the popup

popupTextSmaller.description: Popup button that makes the text smaller

popupTextLarger.description: Popup button that makes the text larger

addressFramesLabel.description: Settings switch: draw a frame around each label of an address

addressFramesDesc.message: Each part of an address gets a frame, heavier on the part that says who owns the site. Off, that part is bold instead.
addressFramesDesc.description: Explanation under the address frames switch

domainMarkerDeepSubdomainsWhy.message: A long chain like this can push the real site name out of view.
domainMarkerDeepSubdomainsWhy.description: Second sentence after "Too many subdomain levels: N", saying why that matters

domainMarkerIpHostWhy.message: There's no site name in it to recognise.
domainMarkerIpHostWhy.description: Second sentence after "Numeric address, not a domain name: 1.2.3.4", saying why that matters

emailFieldSubject.description: Name of the subject field of a mailto link, shown before its value

emailFieldBody.description: Name of the body field of a mailto link (the prefilled message text), shown before its value

emailRemotePublicHint.message: A list you downloaded names this as a public email service, where anyone can register. It's still judged by your visits.
emailRemotePublicHint.description: Under an email address whose domain only the downloaded public-provider list names. The verdict stays the visit-based one: a remote list may add caution, never lift a warning

redFlagsOne.description: Badge beside a verdict: one of the lines under the address is a red flag (drawn with a flag), a reason to stop on its own

redFlagsMany.description: Badge beside a verdict: {n} (2 or more) of the lines under the address are red flags

linkInterceptHeading.message: Stop and ask before opening a link
linkInterceptHeading.description: Heading over the three cases in which a click on a link is held and a dialog asks first

linkInterceptHeadingDesc.message: A dialog shows what Visilant knows about the link before it opens. A link with none of the reasons ticked here opens at once.
linkInterceptHeadingDesc.description: Hint under the heading of the link stop settings

linkInterceptRedFlags.message: When it has {n} or more red flags
linkInterceptRedFlags.description: Checkbox label. {n} is a number box (1 to 5) the user can change, drawn where the placeholder is

linkInterceptRedFlagsDesc.message: A red flag is a trick in the link itself: a decoy name before @, a well-known domain inside another one, mixed alphabets, a bare public IP address, a name made to look like a site you know, or text that names a different site. It stops the link even when it leads somewhere you know.
linkInterceptRedFlagsDesc.description: Hint under the red flags checkbox

linkInterceptShortLinks.message: When it goes through a short-link service

linkInterceptShortLinksDesc.message: A short link hides where it leads. The dialog can follow it and show the real destination.
linkInterceptShortLinksDesc.description: Hint under the short link checkbox

linkInterceptClickAgain.message: This link sits in a separate box on the page, and Visilant can't open it from there. Allowing it opens nothing yet: click the link again within a minute.
linkInterceptClickAgain.description: Link dialog, for a link inside a frame from another site: Allow this link lets the next click on it through, for one minute

linkInterceptShortLinksOwnSite.message: Also on the service's own site
linkInterceptShortLinksOwnSite.description: Settings, under 'short links': whether t.co links on X and the like are stopped too

linkInterceptShortLinksOwnSiteDesc.message: Some sites send every link through their own service, as X does with t.co. Cleared, those links are stopped there only for a red flag.
linkInterceptShortLinksOwnSiteDesc.description: Explanation of the own-site short link setting

linkInterceptUnfamiliar.message: When it leads to an unfamiliar site

linkInterceptUnfamiliarDesc.message: On a page you're new to, this can be most of its links. Without it, an unfamiliar site still warns you once you type there.
linkInterceptUnfamiliarDesc.description: Hint under the unfamiliar site checkbox

linkInterceptTitleRedFlags.description: Title of the link dialog when the click was stopped for red flags in the link, whatever the verdict on the site

listOr.description: Between names in a sentence, every pair of them: paypal.com or google.com or apple.com. Never a comma, which beside an address reads as one of its dots

mailLinkHeading.description: Heading of the tooltip for a mail link that was asked to be checked and names no address

mailLinkNoAddress.message: There's no address in it to check. This is what it holds:
mailLinkNoAddress.description: Under the heading Mail link, above the raw text of a mailto link that names no address, such as mailto:?subject=Hi

helpButtonLabel.description: Name of the question-mark button for a screen reader. What it says is read out after the name

emailForwardingDomain.description: Badge in place of a visit verdict for an address at a mail forwarding service (Firefox Relay, DuckDuckGo Email Protection): a mask over somebody's real address

emailForwardingHint.message: Mail sent to this address is passed on to another mailbox, so the address doesn't say who's behind it.
emailForwardingHint.description: Line under an address at an email forwarding service, the same on every surface

emailCustomForwardingLabel.description: Label for the textarea of the user's own mail forwarding domains

emailCustomForwardingDesc.message: One per line, subdomains included. An address there is shown as an email forwarding service and isn't judged by your visits.
emailCustomForwardingDesc.description: Description for the textarea of the user's own mail forwarding domains

emailHiddenOwnerHelp.message: Writing to it? Whoever gave out this address keeps their real one private, often just to avoid spam, but you can't know who will read your message.
emailHiddenOwnerHelp.description: Behind the question mark on the line about a temporary or a forwarding email service, the same for both and on every surface

emailAddressDetails.description: Button in the tooltip about an email address: opens the check page with the address in it, in a new tab

linkContextMenuMailDetails.message: Address details in a new tab
linkContextMenuMailDetails.description: Context menu item on a mailto link: opens the check page with the link in it, which shows every address the link writes to
